title: Understanding One-hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a way of representing categorical data as binary vectors. Each category is represented by a vector with a single high (1) bit and all other bits low (0).

title: One-hot Encoding of Whole DNA Strings
text: Consider the number of possible DNA strings of length $$3000$$. Each position in the string can be one of $$4$$ letters (T, G, C, A).

title: Calculate Dimensions for Whole DNA Strings
text: Calculate the number of possible DNA strings of length $$3000$$ using one-hot encoding.

title: One-hot Encoding of Codons
text: A codon is a sequence of $$3$$ DNA letters. How many possible codons are there?

title: Calculate Dimensions for Codons
text: Calculate the number of possible codons using one-hot encoding.

title: One-hot Encoding of 6-letter Combos
text: Consider the number of possible 6-letter combinations in a DNA string. Each position can be one of $$4$$ letters.

title: Calculate Dimensions for 6-letter Combos
text: Calculate the number of possible 6-letter combinations using one-hot encoding.

title: Understanding Bags-of-words
text: Bags-of-words encoding involves counting the frequency of each word (or $$n-gram)$$ in a document. In this case, consider the DNA string as a sequence of codons.

title: Calculate Dimensions for Bags-of-words
text: Calculate the number of dimensions for a bags-of-words encoding of codons.
